privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This page explains what NexSift collects and how data is handled, in line with the LGPD.
privacy.productBody: NexSift is an editorial technology intelligence product. There is no login or any form of account; there is no per-user personalization or profile-based recommendations.
privacy.collectBody: NexSift uses PostHog to measure site usage with anonymous events: visited pages, clicks on external sources and navigation actions. The data is aggregated and does not identify you individually. Additionally, when you voluntarily sign up through the updates form, we collect your name and email (and your feedback, if you send it) for the purpose of contacting you and sending updates.
privacy.notCollectBody: We do not collect name, email, ID number, precise location or browsing data outside NexSift, except when you voluntarily sign up through the updates form. We do not use advertising cookies or share data with third parties.
privacy.contentBody: Posts are produced with AI assistance from verified public sources and point to those sources. Verification is automated by the system itself and collects no data from readers. When you access external links, you leave NexSift and become subject to the respective sites' privacy policies.
privacy.retentionBody: Anonymous events are used only to understand product usage and improve the site. Sign-up data is used exclusively for contact and sending updates. There is no profiling, targeted advertising or data selling.
privacy.rightsBody: You may request access, correction or deletion of any data related to you at any time, through the contact email below.
privacy.updated: The current version of this policy is the one published on this page.

about.title: A technical filter, not another infinite feed
about.body: NexSift reduces the cost of keeping up with technology. Instead of reproducing everything, it prioritizes posts with real impact for people who build and operate software.
about.signalBody: A post is a relevant change, verified and placed in context. Not everything that happens is a post: the change must be real, have evidence and alter a decision, risk, opportunity or understanding for people who build or operate technology.
about.criteriaIntro: A post is only published when it passes all of these criteria:
about.criteriaA: Source before opinion: evidence supports every fact, and the source is cited.
about.criteriaB: Context before volume: publishing less is better than lowering the standard.
about.criteriaC: Technical impact before hype: concrete consequence beats flashy novelty.
about.aiBody: AI researches, organizes and drafts with support; NexSift verifies. No claim is published without a verified source, and the text points to the material that supports it. Before making decisions, review the original sources; errors may occur.
about.relevanceBody: Every post gets a relevance (how much it matters to people who build and operate technology) and a confidence (the solidity of the evidence and interpretation). Only posts with relevance 6.5 or above and confidence 7 or above make it to the radar.
about.methodBody: The flow is a sieve: a lot happens, almost nothing gets through. NexSift asks whether the change is real, whether there is evidence and whether it has consequences. What is left becomes a post, and every post ends by indicating what to watch next.
about.creatorTitle: Built by someone who lives the problem
about.creatorBody: NexSift was created by <name>Tiago Castro</name>, a full stack cloud developer with a degree in Systems Analysis and Development and more than 5 years in the market building and operating software. The motivation came from the cost of keeping up with technology: infinite feeds, hype and little context. NexSift is the filter he wanted for himself: few posts, verifiable sources and direct context about what changes for people who build software.
